messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: svc/runner-usw2 scaled group 'inference-pool' experiencing elevated container restarts (oom_kill). metric: restart_count > 20 in last 5m. paging oncall. :rotating_light:

maria: Oncall here, seeing spike. anyone see customer impact?

ashley: CS reporting ~4% errored requests for chats with long contexts (>64k tokens). customers A and B hit failures.

leo: k kubectl get pods -n inference | grep runner-usw2
sam: a few pods in CrashLoopBackOff, recent status OOMKilled.

maria: docs: collect recent pod logs + dmesg from node. @devops-bot can you pull nvidia-smi + dmesg from node runner-23?

devops-bot: fetched artifacts to /artifacts/9170002468/ -> nvidia-smi snapshot, kernel logs, container logs. uploaded.

sam: snippet from container log:
```
2026-03-18T02:41:02Z ERROR model-serving: prefill allocation failed: cudaErrorOutOfMemory: out of memory
stack: runtime.cpp:412 allocate_kv_cache
killed by OOM (PID 7432)
```

leo: k describe pod runner-23-zzzz -n inference shows memory request 0.9Gi but usage spikes to 12Gi during prefill for some requests. Looks like long-context prefill allocations aren't capping.

maria: Immediate mitigations: 1) reduce per-pod max concurrent prefill threads 2) enable stream-trim on long requests 3) shift noisy traffic to dedicated pool (if possible).

ashley: I started a customer-impact note: "We are investigating elevated failures for long context requests. Engineers are mitigating; no data exposure. Updates every 30m." Will send to account teams. :white_check_mark:

leo: rolling a config on inference-config map to set PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=65536 -> 32768 and PREFILL_CONCURRENCY=2 for cluster *usw2*. applying canary to 10% first.

sam: command I ran on canary:
```
k apply -f inference-config-canary.yaml
kubectl rollout restart deployment/runner-canary -n inference
```

maria: monitoring canary. if stable for 10m we promote. watch mem.used and restart_count.

devops-bot: canary deployed. metrics: mem.used per pod down ~40% on canary. restart_count delta -> 0 on canary so far.

leo: also pushed a temporary rate-limiting rule on the gateway for requests with context > 32k tokens: 2r/s per api-key, response 429 with friendly message.

sam: good. that should reduce tail pressure.

maria: escalation decision: no full outage, partial customer impact limited to long-context chats. keep paging local. we will open an incident in status page if customer-facing error rate >5% for 15m. current 4% borderline.

ashley: preparing proactive email for affected customers with workaround (reduce context window or enable streaming mode).

leo: follow-up action items:
- short-term: keep config cap + gateway rate-limit (in place)
- medium-term: add prefill mem accounting + per-request allocation limit in runtime
- long-term: KV cache eviction improvements + better quantization fallback for large contexts

maria: assigning follow-up to engineering backlog: sam (short-term runtime patch), leo (rate-limit doc + telemetry), ashley (customer comms). I'll hand off to oncoming oncall in 30m: @leo take next shift?

leo: taking handoff. will monitor until 11:00 UTC. leaving notes in the runbook: /runbooks/prefill-oom-long-context.md (added canary results and commands).

pagerduty-bot: Incident updated: severity=sev2 -> mitigation in progress, next update 30m.

ashley: sent initial customer note. scheduling update after canary verification.

maria: thanks team. if restarts rise again flip traffic to dedicated-pool-usw2 and escalate to infra.

sam: quick log for postmortem: increased prefetch factor in runtime 02:38 UTC, correlated with the first restarts. reverting prefetch in next deploy.

leo: handing off to @ashley and @sam for customer updates and patch. closing live bridge unless we see new restarts. :handshake:

ashley: closing bridge for now, will reopen if >5% error.
